notes: Original Respond to a Situation items (30 to 90 words each). Questions 31 to 45 are backup questions.

payload.situation: You borrowed a textbook from your classmate, Sam, and accidentally spilled coffee on several pages. Sam needs the book for an exam next week. Explain to Sam what happened and offer a solution.
key_points: explain coffee spilled on the pages
offer to replace or buy a new book

payload.situation: You are working on a group project, but one member, Alex, has not replied to messages for a week and the presentation is in three days. Call Alex, explain your concern and suggest what the group should do next.
key_points: explain the presentation is in three days
concern that Alex has not replied
suggest dividing tasks or meeting soon

payload.situation: You ordered a laptop online for your studies, but it arrived with a cracked screen. Call the store's customer service, describe the problem and explain what you would like them to do.
Your lecturer has scheduled a make-up class at the same time as your part-time job, which you cannot change. Speak to your lecturer, explain the situation and ask about possible alternatives.
key_points: make-up class clashes with part-time job
ask for recording or alternative session

payload.situation: Your flatmate often plays loud music late at night, and you have an important exam tomorrow morning. Talk to your flatmate politely, explain your situation and ask for their cooperation.
key_points: music is loud late at night
ask politely to lower volume or use headphones

payload.situation: You were charged twice for your library fine when you paid online last night. Visit the library help desk, explain what happened and ask the staff member to fix the problem.
key_points: ask for refund of extra payment

payload.situation: A new international student in your class looks confused about how to use the online learning system. Offer to help, explain a few important features and suggest where they can find more support.
key_points: explain how to find course materials and submit assignments
suggest student support or IT help desk

payload.situation: You have been offered a summer internship, but it starts one week before your final exam finishes. Call the employer, thank them for the offer, explain the clash and ask whether the start date could change.
key_points: explain start date clashes with final exam
ask to start one week later

payload.situation: You left your umbrella in a lecture theatre after your economics class yesterday afternoon. Go to the university security office, describe the umbrella and ask whether anyone has handed it in.
key_points: left umbrella in lecture theatre yesterday
ask if it was handed in

payload.situation: Your friend Jordan has invited you to a birthday dinner on Saturday, but you have to finish an assignment due on Monday. Call Jordan, explain why you cannot come and suggest another way to celebrate.
The heater in your student accommodation has stopped working, and the nights have been very cold this week. Call the accommodation manager, describe the problem and ask when it can be repaired.
key_points: ask when it will be repaired

payload.situation: You received a lower mark than expected on an essay, and the feedback does not explain why. Email your tutor to request a meeting, explaining that you want to understand how to improve.
key_points: request meeting to learn how to improve

payload.situation: You are volunteering at a university open day. A parent asks you where the engineering building is and whether there are any tours today. Give clear directions and information about the tours.
You booked a study room for your group, but when you arrive, other students are using it. Speak to them politely, explain that you have a booking and suggest a solution.
key_points: politely explain you booked the room
suggest they find another room or share briefly

payload.situation: Your neighbour's dog has been barking all day while they are at work, and you are trying to study at home. Speak to your neighbour when they return and explain the problem politely.
You need to change your enrolment from one course to another, but the online deadline passed yesterday. Visit the student services office, explain your situation and ask what you can do.
key_points: ask if late change is possible

payload.situation: You are the leader of a study group. One member keeps arriving late and the group is becoming frustrated. Talk to this member privately, explain the effect on the group and agree on a solution.
key_points: group is frustrated and loses time
agree on better meeting time or punctuality

payload.situation: You bought a monthly bus pass, but the bus route to campus has been cancelled for road works for three weeks. Call the transport company, explain the situation and ask for compensation.
Your manager at your part-time job has asked you to work extra shifts during your exam period. Speak to your manager, explain why this is difficult and suggest a compromise.
key_points: offer fewer shifts or work after exams

payload.situation: A classmate asks to copy your completed assignment because they did not have time to finish theirs. Respond to your classmate, explain why you cannot share it and offer another kind of help.
key_points: offer to help explain topic or ask for extension

payload.situation: You are presenting in class, but the projector is not working and your slides cannot be shown. Explain the problem to the audience and describe how you will continue your presentation.
key_points: continue by speaking from notes or sharing slides later

payload.situation: You have been feeling very stressed about your studies and have not been sleeping well. Call the university counselling service, explain how you are feeling and ask about making an appointment.
You arrive at a restaurant for a booking you made for a friend's farewell dinner, but the staff cannot find your reservation. Speak to the manager, explain the situation and ask for help.
key_points: made a booking for farewell dinner
ask manager for a table or solution

payload.situation: Your research supervisor has asked you to present your results at a department meeting next week, but your data analysis is not finished. Speak to your supervisor, explain your progress and suggest options.
key_points: suggest presenting preliminary results or later date

payload.situation: You found a wallet containing cash and a student ID card on a bench outside the library. Take it to the campus security office and explain where and when you found it.
key_points: explain time and place and hand it in

payload.situation: You want to join the university hiking club, but the membership fee is higher than you can afford this month. Speak to the club president and ask whether there are any payment options.
key_points: ask about payment plan or discount

payload.situation: Your landlord has told you that your rent will increase next month, but your lease says the rent is fixed for the year. Call your landlord, refer to the lease and explain your position calmly.
key_points: lease says rent is fixed for the year
calmly ask to keep current rent

payload.situation: You are sick with a high fever on the day of a tutorial presentation. Call your tutor, explain your illness and ask whether you can present on a different day.
key_points: ask to present another day and provide medical certificate

payload.situation: A tourist stops you in the city centre and asks how to get to the art gallery. You know the gallery is a ten-minute walk away. Give clear directions and mention a useful landmark.
You are organising a charity event on campus, and the guest speaker has just cancelled. Call a lecturer you know, explain the situation and ask whether they could speak at the event instead.
The washing machine in your shared house broke after you used it, and your housemates think you damaged it. Talk to your housemates, explain what happened and suggest how to fix the problem.
key_points: suggest calling repair service and sharing cost

payload.situation: You signed up for a free trial of a study app, but you were charged a monthly fee without warning. Call customer support, explain what happened and ask for a refund.
Your classmate missed today's biology lecture because of illness and asks you what was covered. Summarise the main topics briefly and tell them where they can find the lecture slides.
You ordered a vegetarian meal for a university conference dinner, but you were served a meat dish. Speak to the waiter politely, explain the mistake and ask for the correct meal.
You have been asked to lead a new student orientation tour, but you have never done it before. Speak to the coordinator, explain your concerns and ask what information and support you will receive.
key_points: ask for training and route information

payload.situation: Your new phone's screen cracked one week after you bought it, even though you did not drop it. Return to the shop, explain what happened and ask about the warranty.
You notice that a group of students is leaving rubbish in the campus garden after lunch every day. Speak to them politely, explain why this is a problem and suggest what they could do instead.
key_points: explain effect on environment and others

payload.situation: You need a reference letter for a scholarship application due in five days. Speak to a lecturer who taught you last year, explain the scholarship and politely ask whether they could write the letter.
key_points: politely ask lecturer for reference letter

payload.situation: You accidentally took a classmate's calculator home after this morning's statistics exam, and they need it for another exam tomorrow. Call your classmate, apologise and arrange a time to return it.
The Wi-Fi in the library keeps disconnecting, and you cannot submit your online quiz. Go to the IT help desk, describe the problem and ask for help before the quiz closes.
key_points: ask for urgent help or extension

payload.situation: You disagree with a decision your group made about the topic for your research project. At the next meeting, explain your view respectfully and suggest a way the group could reach agreement.
You have been waiting forty minutes for a doctor's appointment at the campus clinic, and you have a class starting soon. Speak to the receptionist, explain your situation and ask about your options.
key_points: ask how long or to rebook

payload.situation: A close friend has asked you for advice because they are thinking about dropping out of university after failing one course this semester. Give your friend some encouragement and practical suggestions.
key_points: encourage friend not to give up
one failed course is not the end
suggest talking to adviser or getting tutoring

payload.situation: You are at a café and realise you left your wallet at home after ordering your coffee. Explain the situation to the staff member and suggest a way to pay.
key_points: offer to pay by phone or return later

payload.situation: You are sharing a car ride to campus with three classmates, but one person is always late, making everyone miss the start of class. Speak to the group and suggest a fair solution.
